description: Dependency-free .NET 8 APIs for binary files, streams, readers and writers, compression, storage, and file-system observation.
executionSupportMessage: Compatible with the built-in .NET 10 C# runner; authored against .NET 8.

actionDescriptions.Compress: Encodes data into a smaller representation using a compression algorithm.
actionDescriptions.Convert: Changes a value into another representation or data type.
actionDescriptions.Copy: Copies bytes, values, or resources to another destination.
actionDescriptions.Create: Constructs a new object, resource, or language structure.
actionDescriptions.Decompress: Restores compressed data to its uncompressed representation.
actionDescriptions.Format: Creates a particular textual or binary representation of a value.
actionDescriptions.Get: Retrieves information without intentionally changing the source.
actionDescriptions.Read: Reads text, bytes, messages, or values from a source.
actionDescriptions.Write: Writes text, bytes, messages, or values to a destination.

objectDescriptions.Binary file: A binary file stores bytes whose interpretation is defined by an image, archive, executable, protocol, or application-specific format.
objectDescriptions.Binary value: A binary value is a typed primitive or string represented as bytes in a documented byte order and encoding.
objectDescriptions.Directory: A directory is a file-system container that can contain files and nested directories.
objectDescriptions.Directory archive: A directory archive stores a directory tree and its file contents inside one compressed container.
objectDescriptions.Directory watcher: A directory watcher subscribes to operating-system notifications for matching file-system changes.
objectDescriptions.Drive: A drive represents a mounted or logical storage volume visible to the operating system.
objectDescriptions.File attributes: File attributes are bit flags describing file-system traits such as hidden, read-only, directory, archive, or reparse-point state.
objectDescriptions.File stream: A FileStream provides seekable or sequential byte access backed by an operating-system file handle.
objectDescriptions.Memory stream: A MemoryStream provides seekable byte access backed by managed memory instead of a file or network resource.
objectDescriptions.Path: A path is text identifying a file-system location; Path helpers transform that text without opening the target.
objectDescriptions.Stream: A Stream is the .NET abstraction for reading, writing, and seeking through a sequence of bytes.
objectDescriptions.Text stream: A text stream decodes or encodes characters over an underlying byte stream with a selected text encoding.

commands.name: File.ReadAllBytesAsync
commands.description: Read an entire file into a byte array asynchronously.
commands.definition: Opens a file, asynchronously reads all of its bytes, closes the file, and returns the completed byte array. Large files are usually better processed as streams.

examples.title: Calculate a binary file size
examples.code:
var bytes = await File.ReadAllBytesAsync("icon.png");
Console.WriteLine($"Loaded {bytes.Length:N0} bytes.");
examples.explanation: The complete file is available in memory after the awaited operation finishes.

commands.name: File.WriteAllBytesAsync
commands.description: Write a complete byte array to a file asynchronously.
commands.definition: Creates or overwrites a file, asynchronously writes the supplied bytes, and closes the file when the operation completes.

parameters.name: bytes
parameters.description: The byte array or compatible memory to write.

examples.title: Persist decoded data
examples.code:
var bytes = Convert.FromBase64String("SHlwZXJzaGVsbA==");
await File.WriteAllBytesAsync("payload.bin", bytes);
examples.explanation: The decoded bytes replace payload.bin, creating it when necessary.

commands.name: File.OpenRead
commands.description: Open an existing file as a read-only stream.
commands.definition: Opens a FileStream for reading with sharing that permits other readers. The returned stream must be disposed.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The existing file path to open.

examples.title: Read a file header
examples.explanation: Only the first bytes are loaded, and the using declaration closes the file reliably.

commands.name: File.OpenWrite
commands.description: Open or create a file as a writable stream.
commands.definition: Opens an existing file or creates a new one for writing. The stream begins at position zero but does not automatically truncate existing trailing content.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file path to open or create.

examples.title: Write a compact binary header
examples.explanation: SetLength removes old trailing bytes before the new header is written.

commands.name: Stream.CopyToAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously copy all remaining bytes between streams.
commands.definition: Reads from the source stream's current position and writes to the destination until the source reaches its end. Neither stream is disposed by the operation.

examples.title: Copy one file to another through streams
examples.explanation: The copy is streamed instead of loading the complete input into memory.

commands.name: Stream.ReadExactlyAsync
commands.description: Fill a buffer asynchronously or fail at end of stream.
commands.definition: Repeatedly reads until the requested buffer is full. It throws EndOfStreamException when the source ends before all requested bytes arrive.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.description: The buffer that must be completely filled.

examples.title: Read a fixed-size protocol header
examples.explanation: The call either fills all eight bytes or reports a truncated input instead of returning a partial header.

commands.name: StreamReader.ReadLineAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously read the next text line.
commands.definition: Reads characters through the next line terminator and returns the line without that terminator. It returns null after the final line.

examples.title: Process a text file line by line
examples.explanation: Only one line is retained at a time, and the null pattern ends the loop at end of file.

commands.name: StreamReader.ReadToEndAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously read all remaining text.
commands.definition: Reads from the current position through the end of the text stream and returns one string. Streaming is preferable when the remaining content may be large.

examples.title: Decode UTF-8 text from a stream
examples.explanation: StreamReader handles byte-to-character decoding while the awaited call collects the remaining characters.

commands.name: StreamWriter.WriteLineAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously write text followed by a line terminator.
commands.definition: Writes the supplied text and the writer's line terminator without synchronously blocking for the underlying destination.

examples.title: Append a timestamped log line
examples.code:
await using var writer = new StreamWriter("events.log", append: true);
await writer.WriteLineAsync($"{DateTimeOffset.UtcNow:O} build completed");
examples.explanation: Disposing the writer flushes its encoding buffer after the asynchronous write.

commands.name: MemoryStream.ToArray
commands.description: Copy a memory stream's contents into a byte array.
commands.definition: Returns a new byte array containing the bytes written to the stream, regardless of its current Position. The returned array is independent of the stream.

examples.title: Build a binary payload in memory
examples.explanation: ToArray returns every written byte even though the stream position is at its end.

commands.name: BinaryReader.ReadInt32
commands.description: Read a little-endian 32-bit integer from a stream.
commands.definition: Reads four bytes from the underlying stream and interprets them as a signed Int32 using BinaryReader's fixed binary representation.

examples.title: Read a binary record count
examples.explanation: The four little-endian bytes are interpreted as the integer 3.

commands.name: BinaryWriter.Write
commands.description: Write a typed primitive or string in binary form.
commands.definition: Writes a supported primitive, byte sequence, character sequence, or string to the underlying stream using BinaryWriter's documented representation.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The strongly typed value to encode.

examples.title: Create a small binary record
examples.explanation: The writer encodes the integer and length-prefixed string into the same memory stream.

commands.name: ZipFile.CreateFromDirectory
commands.description: Create a ZIP archive from a directory tree.
commands.definition: Recursively compresses a source directory into a new ZIP archive. The destination archive must not already exist unless the caller removes or replaces it first.

parameters.name: sourceDirectory
parameters.description: The directory whose contents will be archived.

examples.title: Archive a build output directory
examples.explanation: An existing archive is removed explicitly before the directory tree is compressed.

commands.name: ZipFile.ExtractToDirectory
commands.description: Extract a ZIP archive into a directory.
commands.definition: Expands archive entries beneath a destination directory. An overload can overwrite existing files; untrusted archives require additional policy around paths, size, and content.

examples.title: Extract into a fresh temporary directory
examples.explanation: A unique destination avoids collisions with files from an earlier extraction.

commands.name: GZipStream.Compress
commands.description: Compress one stream into GZip format.
commands.definition: A GZipStream in Compress mode writes a GZip-formatted byte stream to its destination. Disposing it finalizes the compression footer.
commands.template:
await using var gzip = new GZipStream({destination}, CompressionLevel.Optimal, leaveOpen: true);
await {source}.CopyToAsync(gzip);

examples.title: Compress a file
examples.explanation: The nested using scope finalizes GZip metadata before the destination file is closed.

commands.name: GZipStream.Decompress
commands.description: Decompress a GZip stream.
commands.definition: A GZipStream in Decompress mode exposes the uncompressed bytes read from an underlying GZip-formatted source.
commands.template:
await using var gzip = new GZipStream({source}, CompressionMode.Decompress, leaveOpen: true);
await gzip.CopyToAsync({destination});

examples.title: Restore a compressed file
examples.explanation: Copying from the decompression stream writes restored bytes to the destination.

commands.name: FileSystemWatcher.Create
commands.description: Watch a directory for selected file-system changes.
commands.definition: FileSystemWatcher raises events for matching changes reported by the operating system. Event bursts, duplicate events, buffer overflow, and race conditions must be handled by production consumers.

examples.title: Observe JSON changes briefly
examples.explanation: The watcher remains alive for ten seconds; real applications normally tie its lifetime to a longer-running service.

commands.name: DriveInfo.GetDrives
commands.description: Get the logical drives visible to the current machine.
commands.definition: Returns DriveInfo objects for mounted or logical drives. Some properties can throw when a drive is unavailable or not ready.

examples.title: Report ready drive space
examples.explanation: IsReady is checked before querying format and capacity properties.

commands.name: Path.GetRelativePath
commands.description: Calculate a relative path between two absolute path contexts.
commands.definition: Resolves both inputs and returns a path that reaches the target from the base path according to platform path-comparison rules.

examples.title: Create a project-relative label
examples.explanation: The result describes the target beneath the project root without retaining the absolute prefix.

commands.name: File.GetAttributes
commands.description: Read a file or directory's attribute flags.
commands.definition: Returns a bitwise FileAttributes value describing flags such as Directory, Hidden, ReadOnly, Archive, and ReparsePoint.

examples.title: Test whether a path is hidden
examples.explanation: FileAttributes is a flags enum, so HasFlag tests one bit without discarding the others.
